findings.title: No privacy policy page found
findings.description: No file or route resembling a privacy policy was detected. Apps that collect user data need a published, accessible privacy policy.
findings.remediation: Add `/privacy` (or similar) describing what data you collect, why, how long it's retained, third parties it's shared with, and how users can export/delete it.

findings.title: No terms of service found
findings.description: No file or route resembling Terms of Service was detected. Public-facing apps should publish ToS limiting liability and defining acceptable use.
findings.remediation: Add `/terms` covering acceptable use, liability disclaimers, dispute resolution, and termination conditions.

manualChecklist.item: List every third party that receives user data (analytics, error reporting, LLM providers, payment processors)
manualChecklist.rationale: Required for GDPR/CCPA disclosure and Data Processing Agreements.

manualChecklist.item: Define data retention windows per data type
manualChecklist.rationale: Indefinite retention is hostile to user privacy and increases breach blast radius.

manualChecklist.item: Verify Data Processing Agreement (DPA) signed with each sub-processor
manualChecklist.rationale: GDPR Article 28 requires DPAs with processors handling personal data.

manualChecklist.item: Cookie banner / consent management is wired (if EU/UK users)
manualChecklist.rationale: GDPR + ePrivacy Directive require informed consent for non-essential cookies.

manualChecklist.item: Privacy policy lists all processors + retention windows + lawful basis
manualChecklist.rationale: Plain-language disclosure is legally required, not optional.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm publishable/anon keys are documented as intentionally-public by the provider
manualChecklist.rationale: Some 'public' keys are safe to expose (Stripe publishable, Supabase anon); others are not.

manualChecklist.item: Verify credential rotation cadence is defined and tested
manualChecklist.rationale: Even unleaked credentials should be rotated periodically.

manualChecklist.item: Check provider audit logs for unexpected access
manualChecklist.rationale: Past leaks may have been exploited.

manualChecklist.item: Test ownership boundaries — sign in as user A, try to access user B's resources via direct URL
manualChecklist.rationale: BOLA / IDOR is the #1 API vuln per OWASP API Top 10 2023.

manualChecklist.item: Verify MFA is available (and required for admin)
manualChecklist.rationale: Compromised passwords are the most common breach vector.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm session timeout + inactivity logout exists
manualChecklist.rationale: Long-lived sessions on shared/public devices are a leak path.

manualChecklist.item: Check rate limit on login + password reset endpoints
manualChecklist.rationale: Credential stuffing & enumeration require throttling.

manualChecklist.item: Verify every state-changing endpoint requires POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE (not GET)
manualChecklist.rationale: GET requests are logged in browser history, referrer headers, and CDN logs.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm OpenAPI/Swagger spec exists and matches implementation
manualChecklist.rationale: Drift between docs and code hides shadow endpoints.

manualChecklist.item: Test rate limits return 429 with a Retry-After header
manualChecklist.rationale: Some implementations silently drop; clients need feedback.

findings.title: Security header missing or malformed: strict-transport-security
findings.description: HSTS — forces HTTPS, prevents downgrade attacks. Header was not set.
findings.remediation: Set `strict-transport-security` at your reverse proxy / framework. See `references/tool-reference.md` for production-grade values.

findings.title: Security header missing or malformed: content-security-policy
findings.description: CSP — defence-in-depth against XSS and data injection. Header was not set.
findings.remediation: Set `content-security-policy` at your reverse proxy / framework. See `references/tool-reference.md` for production-grade values.

manualChecklist.item: Threat-model the auth boundary: what does a malicious authenticated user gain access to?
manualChecklist.rationale: OWASP A04 (Insecure Design) cannot be detected by scanners — needs human judgement.

manualChecklist.item: Review every dependency added in the last 6 months for typosquatting / abandoned-maintainer risk
manualChecklist.rationale: Supply-chain attacks (A08) target recently-added or unmaintained packages.

manualChecklist.item: Run a real DAST (ZAP full scan) at least once before launch and after every major release
manualChecklist.rationale: Static analysis cannot replicate exploit paths.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm a per-tenant daily/monthly cost cap is enforced at the application layer
manualChecklist.rationale: Rate limits alone don't prevent a single bad actor from draining a budget within their quota.

manualChecklist.item: Bot/CAPTCHA on signup + login + 'forgot password'
manualChecklist.rationale: Most abuse arrives via cheap-account creation.

manualChecklist.item: Billing-anomaly alert wired to ops channel
manualChecklist.rationale: Catch runaway costs in minutes not days.

findings.title: Internal URL / IP hardcoded in source
findings.description: Hard-coded internal hostnames or IPs end up in the production bundle and may reveal architecture details to attackers.
findings.remediation: Move URLs to environment-driven config. Verify the build pipeline strips dev-only paths.

manualChecklist.item: Open DevTools → Network tab on the production app — is any request going to a dev/staging URL?
manualChecklist.rationale: AI-generated code commonly leaves mixed-environment URLs after a copy-paste.

manualChecklist.item: Check the bundle for comments / console.log statements
manualChecklist.rationale: Debug output may leak request/response shapes and PII.

findings.title: Sensitive field referenced in a log/print call
findings.description: A log statement appears to include an authorization header, token, password, or API key. Secrets in logs end up in centralized log stores, support tools, and accidentally in screenshots.
findings.remediation: Use a redaction layer (e.g., pino redact, structlog processors). Log only field names + a hash if you need to correlate. Treat `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `password`, `token`, `secret`, `api_key` as never-loggable.

findings.title: High volume of ad-hoc log statements (console.log: 152, print: 0)
findings.description: AI-generated code routinely leaves debug `console.log` / `print` calls in place. They produce log noise, may leak data, and cost CPU on hot paths.
findings.remediation: Adopt a structured logger (pino, winston, structlog, loguru). Strip / lint console.log in production builds (`no-console` ESLint rule).

manualChecklist.item: Verify centralized logs are searchable for at least 7 days
manualChecklist.rationale: Incidents are often noticed after they end; you need retention to retro.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm uptime monitor with on-call paging (StatusCake / BetterStack / Pingdom)
manualChecklist.rationale: External probe catches what your internal metrics can't.

manualChecklist.rationale: Required for SOC 2 + GDPR + breach forensics.

manualChecklist.rationale: An untested rollback is a hope, not a plan.

manualChecklist.rationale: Prefer sharp / pillow over ImageMagick if possible.

manualChecklist.item: Database admin password rotation policy + last rotation date

manualChecklist.item: Audit log captures: schema changes, role grants, admin queries, data exports
manualChecklist.rationale: Required for SOC 2 + breach forensics.

manualChecklist.rationale: AI-generated migrations frequently aren't reversible.

findings.title: Type-checker suppression

findings.remediation: Either fix the underlying type problem or add a justification comment with an issue number to track removal.

findings.description: MD5 and SHA1 are cryptographically broken. Do not use for passwords, signatures, or integrity.
findings.remediation: Use SHA-256+ for hashing, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords, HMAC-SHA256 for signing.

findings.title: Read-modify-write with no transaction / optimistic lock
findings.description: This module reads a record and later writes it back without any transaction, `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, or version column. Two concurrent writers can each read the old value and clobber each other — a classic lost update.
findings.impact: Silent data loss under concurrency: balances, counters, and inventory drift when two requests race.
findings.remediation: Wrap the read-modify-write in a transaction, or use an optimistic-lock version column and retry on conflict, or push the mutation into a single atomic SQL statement (`UPDATE … SET x = x + 1`).

manualChecklist.item: Double-submit every create/pay/delete action (click twice fast, and retry on a flaky network) — confirm exactly one side effect
manualChecklist.rationale: Idempotency and in-flight guards can only be confirmed by exercising the real flow.

manualChecklist.item: Open the app in two tabs, edit the same record in both, save both — confirm the second save is rejected or merged, not silently lost
manualChecklist.rationale: Lost-update / optimistic-lock behaviour is invisible to static analysis.

manualChecklist.item: Fire two requests that depend on ordering (e.g. create then immediately update) and confirm out-of-order arrival is handled
manualChecklist.rationale: Request ordering / race conditions surface only under real latency.

manualChecklist.item: Trigger a provider webhook twice with the same event id — confirm the second is a no-op (dedupe by event id)
manualChecklist.rationale: Webhook redelivery is guaranteed by most providers; duplicate processing corrupts state.

manualChecklist.item: Kill the process mid-write (or simulate it) and confirm no partially-written / torn state remains on restart
manualChecklist.rationale: Atomic-write / crash-consistency guarantees need a fault-injection test.

manualChecklist.item: Tab through every interactive element — confirm hover, focus-visible, active, and disabled states all exist and are distinct
manualChecklist.rationale: AI-generated components routinely ship only the default state; missing focus rings also fail accessibility.

manualChecklist.item: Shrink to 320px and grow to 1440px+ — confirm no horizontal scroll, clipped text, or overlapping elements at any breakpoint
manualChecklist.rationale: Overflow and breakpoint gaps are perceptual and not detectable by grep.

manualChecklist.item: Render the loading, empty, error, and success state of every data view — confirm all four are designed, not just the happy path
manualChecklist.rationale: Empty/error/loading states are the most commonly missing screens in AI-built UIs.

manualChecklist.item: Compare headings, body, and captions across 3+ screens — confirm one consistent type scale, not per-screen font sizes
manualChecklist.rationale: Typography drift is obvious to users but invisible to static checks.

manualChecklist.item: Fill fields with the longest realistic content (long names, long i18n strings, big numbers) — confirm nothing truncates or breaks layout
manualChecklist.rationale: Localization/content expansion (German, etc.) breaks fixed-width layouts.

manualChecklist.item: Spot-check that repeated components (buttons, cards, inputs) use one shared variant, not divergent one-off copies
manualChecklist.rationale: Component-variant drift accumulates silently across a codebase.

findings.title: No JSON-LD structured data detected
findings.description: No `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks found. JSON-LD is the recommended format for Schema.org markup. It is not a ranking factor, but valid structured data that matches visible content enables rich results and helps answer engines interpret entities. Do not add schema that does not match the visible page.
findings.remediation: If the page represents a clear entity (Article, Product, Organization, FAQ, BreadcrumbList), add matching JSON-LD that mirrors visible content. Validate with the Rich Results Test.

findings.title: robots.txt declares no sitemap
findings.description: No `Sitemap:` directive in robots.txt. Sitemaps are not required, but they help crawlers discover URLs (especially new, isolated, or JS-rendered pages). For multi-page sites, declare at least one.
findings.remediation: Generate a sitemap.xml and reference it via `Sitemap: <absolute-url>` in robots.txt. Many frameworks auto-generate this.

manualChecklist.item: Decide and document AI-bot policy (training vs search vs user-fetch)
manualChecklist.rationale: robots.txt has no explicit AI-bot directives, meaning all AI crawlers are allowed by default (per RFC 9309, omission = allow). The owner should consciously decide whether training crawlers (GPTBot, CCBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended) are permitted and set directives accordingly. This is a policy decision, not a defect.

manualChecklist.item: Verify rendered-vs-raw HTML parity (Lighthouse unavailable)
manualChecklist.rationale: Lighthouse is not installed, so this audit could not run a headless render. For JS-heavy sites, the raw-curl HTML may differ from what a rendered crawler sees. Manually fetch the page with JS disabled and compare — if title/canonical/content are missing without JS, the site is not reliably indexable.

manualChecklist.item: Verify index coverage and canonical selection in Search Console / Bing Webmaster Tools
manualChecklist.rationale: Automation can detect directives but cannot see actual index status, canonical selection, or crawl frequency. These are observable only in first-party console data. Check the URL Inspection tool for the audit URL.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm structured data (if present) matches visible page content
manualChecklist.rationale: Schema that does not mirror visible content is a spam signal and can trigger manual action. The Rich Results Test validates syntax; only a human can confirm semantic match against the rendered page.

manualChecklist.rationale: Component-variant drift accumulates silently across a codebase.

manualChecklist.item: Decide and document AI-bot policy (training vs search vs user-fetch)
manualChecklist.rationale: robots.txt has no explicit AI-bot directives, meaning all AI crawlers are allowed by default (per RFC 9309, omission = allow). The owner should consciously decide whether training crawlers (GPTBot, CCBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended) are permitted and set directives accordingly. This is a policy decision, not a defect.

manualChecklist.item: Verify rendered-vs-raw HTML parity (Lighthouse unavailable)
manualChecklist.rationale: Lighthouse is not installed, so this audit could not run a headless render. For JS-heavy sites, the raw-curl HTML may differ from what a rendered crawler sees. Manually fetch the page with JS disabled and compare — if title/canonical/content are missing without JS, the site is not reliably indexable.

manualChecklist.item: Verify index coverage and canonical selection in Search Console / Bing Webmaster Tools
manualChecklist.rationale: Automation can detect directives but cannot see actual index status, canonical selection, or crawl frequency. These are observable only in first-party console data. Check the URL Inspection tool for the audit URL.

manualChecklist.item: Confirm structured data (if present) matches visible page content
manualChecklist.rationale: Schema that does not mirror visible content is a spam signal and can trigger manual action. The Rich Results Test validates syntax; only a human can confirm semantic match against the rendered page.
